newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Army hunts combat plane lost over Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Army hunts combat plane lost over Colombia.

text.p: Troops combed the remote jungle-covered mountains of northwest Colombia on Monday after a combat aircraft disappeared during an anti-guerrilla mission, a military spokesman said.
The plane, a U.S.-made A-37, was flying at 13,000 feet (4,000 metres) on a reconnaissance mission over the banana-growing region of Uraba on Sunday afternoon when it apparently crashed.

A spokesman for the army's Seventeenth Brigade said neither the pilot, who was the lone crew member on board, nor the plane had been located. He said the presence of leftist guerrillas in the area was hampering the search operation.
He said it was unlikely the plane had been shot down and said a mechanical fault probably caused the accident.

The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's largest guerrilla force, has been active in the region in the last two weeks and set up a partial blockade of the main highway into Uraba.
